eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Temporary Regulation on Voluntary Detection of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM):** Online communication service providers offering number-independent interpersonal communication services can now voluntarily detect, remove, and report child sexual abuse material on their platforms until April 3, 2028. Previously, the interim derogation from EU privacy rules that allowed such voluntary detection expired on April 3, 2026, creating a legal gap. This new regulation explicitly excludes communications protected by end-to-end encryption (e.g., WhatsApp, Signal) from its scope. This restores a legal basis for platforms to continue vital CSAM detection efforts while safeguarding the privacy of end-to-end encrypted communications.

• **21st Package of Restrictive Measures against Russia:** The Council adopted a new package of economic and individual sanctions on July 23, 2026. Previously, existing sanctions were in place. The new measures include asset freezes and transaction bans on 94 additional Russian banks and financial institutions, extending existing bans to 33 more, and imposing transaction bans on a Kyrgyz bank and three other non-Russian banks for sanctions circumvention. A new instrument now allows the EU to ban any transaction between an EU operator and any crypto provider used by Russia. Furthermore, it introduces a comprehensive visa ban for Russian combatants and ex-combatants. This significantly broadens the scope of EU sanctions, further restricting Russia's economy and its ability to fund its war of aggression, impacting EU financial institutions, crypto service providers, and businesses.

• **Commission Decision Fining Google for Digital Markets Act (DMA) Breaches:** The European Commission fined Google €890 million (approximately $1.013 billion) on July 24, 2026, for non-compliance with the Digital Markets Act (DMA). Previously, under the DMA, designated "gatekeepers" like Google were prohibited from giving preferential treatment to their own services and were required to allow app developers to inform users of alternative offers. Google was found to be giving preferential treatment to its own services (such as shopping, hotels, transport, and sports results) in Google Search and restricting app developers from guiding customers to alternative, potentially cheaper, offers outside Google Play. This decision mandates structural changes to Google's advertising, search, and app ecosystems in Europe, promoting fair competition and potentially benefiting smaller businesses and consumers.

Why it matters: This week saw significant EU action in digital policy, foreign relations, and competition, with the reinforcement of child protection measures alongside strong privacy safeguards for encrypted communications, a substantial expansion of sanctions against Russia, and a landmark fine against Google enforcing fair competition in digital markets.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **Middle East Conflict & Global Oil Markets:** The ongoing conflict escalated significantly on July 24, 2026, with the US military conducting its 13th consecutive night of airstrikes on Iran, while Iran retaliated with missile and drone attacks targeting US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and the Al-Azraq airbase in Jordan. Simultaneously, Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, causing one vessel to catch fire. This renewed escalation, following the collapse of a ceasefire, drove Brent crude oil prices up by $6.58, or 6.96%, to $100.65 a barrel, marking the first time prices have exceeded $100 since May. US President Donald Trump stated that he had not decided on launching "major strikes" but warned Iran could face a "much higher level" of attacks if it did not get "serious" in talks, despite Human Rights Watch warning both sides against targeting civilian infrastructure. The widening conflict and threats to crucial shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea pose significant risks to global energy supplies and international trade, impacting oil prices and potentially contributing to inflation and economic instability worldwide.

• **US Global Tariffs:** On July 24, 2026, the US administration under President Donald Trump imposed new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 global economies, including major trading partners like the European Union and China. These new duties replaced temporary 10% levies under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 that expired on the same day. The US justified these tariffs by alleging a lack of enforcement of forced labor laws in these countries, an accusation strongly rejected by many affected nations, including EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, who asserted the EU possesses stronger labor laws. This move significantly deepens President Trump's global trade war, potentially triggering retaliatory tariffs from countries like Brazil, which is considering action and a World Trade Organization complaint. The tariffs are expected to increase costs for businesses and consumers globally, contributing to inflation and creating uncertainty in international trade relations, with an immediate impact seen in stock market jitters.

• **Israeli-Palestinian Conflict:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the establishment of new settler outposts in the occupied West Bank on July 24, 2026, as a retaliatory measure after a deadly confrontation near the Havat Gilad settlement and the neighboring Palestinian village of Tell. The violence resulted in the deaths of four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers. This development exacerbates the already surging violence in the West Bank since the October 7, 2023, Gaza war, during which at least 1,094 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers. The order for new settlements signals a further entrenchment of Israeli control over disputed territories, undermining prospects for a two-state solution and raising international condemnation and humanitarian concerns for Palestinian populations.

• **ICC Chief Prosecutor Removal:** Karim Khan, the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and a British barrister, was removed from office on July 24, 2026, by a vote of the court's 125-member states. His ouster, which came nearly two years after sexual misconduct allegations against him first emerged, was for "serious misconduct and serious breach of duty." This removal significantly impacts the leadership and credibility of the world's only permanent court for prosecuting war crimes, genocide, and crimes against humanity. It occurs amid existing challenges, including a campaign by the United States to "dismantle" the ICC and sanctions imposed by the Trump administration against Khan and other staff over warrants issued for top Israeli officials.

• **European Wildfires:** Wildfires continued to rage across parts of Europe on July 24, 2026, with southwestern France being particularly affected as flames swept through the Cap Ferret peninsula, forcing the evacuation of over 20,000 tourists and residents. Spain's Madrid region also declared a state of emergency due to wildfires, prompting France to seek emergency assistance from the European Union. These fires are linked to increasingly common extreme weather episodes, including three heatwaves that have battered France since May. The widespread wildfires represent a significant humanitarian crisis, displacing tens of thousands, destroying property, and severely impacting tourism and local economies across affected European nations, while underscoring the escalating real-world global impact of climate change.

Why it matters: Today's global events highlight intensifying geopolitical conflicts and economic protectionism, driving instability in critical energy markets and trade relations, alongside escalating humanitarian crises exacerbated by climate change and persistent regional disputes challenging international justice institutions.

investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS
*   **Equities & Indices — Tesla:** Tesla shares plunged after reporting disappointing Q2 2026 earnings, with an adjusted EPS of $0.33 significantly missing analyst estimates of $0.54, a collapse in operating margin to 1.4%, and negative free cash flow. This was further exacerbated by a substantial increase in capital expenditures on AI and robotics, coupled with delays in key projects like its Robotaxi service. This signals increasing investor scrutiny on the profitability and execution timelines of significant AI and innovation investments, directly impacting Pedro's tech holdings.

*   **Equities & Indices — Alphabet:** Despite strong Q2 2026 revenue that beat expectations, Alphabet's stock experienced a sharp decline following its earnings call. Investors reacted negatively to the company's raised 2026 AI capital expenditure guidance to $205 billion, up from $180 billion, and its first-time reporting of negative free cash flow. This indicates market concern over the immediate return on substantial AI infrastructure investments, impacting sentiment for other large tech and AI players.

*   **Aerospace & Defense (ITA ETF):** The sector received a boost from new contract awards and investment announcements. Rockwell Collins ESA Vision Systems, in collaboration with RTX, secured a $332.6 million U.S. defense contract to provide spare parts and repair services for the Joint Helmet Mounted Cueing System used in F-15, F-16, and F-18 fighter jets. Additionally, Electra announced an $850 million manufacturing plant in Ohio for hybrid-electric aircraft, and ParaZero Technologies received a new order for its DefendAir Net Pod system for Counter-UAS applications from an Israeli defense company. These developments indicate robust government and private sector investment in defense and aerospace innovation.

*   **Oil & Gas:** WTI oil prices pulled back today due to profit-taking, but maintained strong weekly gains fueled by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and renewed threats from President Trump against Iran significantly raised concerns over global supply security earlier in the week, alongside production reductions in Kazakhstan. This volatility highlights the ongoing impact of geopolitical risks on global energy supply and pricing.

*   **Crypto:** Global regulatory scrutiny on digital assets is intensifying. The European Union adopted its 21st sanctions package against Russia, directly targeting over 100 banks and crypto operators involved in sanctions evasion, imposing transaction bans on 14 crypto platforms and introducing a mechanism for full third-country bans on crypto-asset services. Concurrently, SEC Commissioner Hester M. Peirce issued a statement highlighting that crypto vaults and on-chain lending strategies may fall under federal securities laws. Momentum is also building in the US for the CLARITY Act, aiming to establish a comprehensive digital asset market structure. These actions underscore a global trend towards increased oversight and compliance requirements for digital assets.

Why it matters: Investor focus is sharply shifting towards demonstrated returns on massive AI investments, with substantial capital expenditure and project delays in tech giants leading to significant market corrections, while geopolitical tensions continue to fuel volatility in energy and drive sustained spending in defense.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Reforma da Justiça Administrativa e Fiscal:** O Conselho de Ministros aprovou um conjunto de diplomas destinados a desburocratizar e agilizar a justiça administrativa e fiscal. Inclui a criação de uma Câmara de Resolução de Litígios de Contratação Pública, respostas especializadas para processos de imigração e proteção internacional, e um novo procedimento administrativo para cidadãos pedirem indemnizações ao Estado por prejuízos causados pela Administração Pública. Anteriormente, os cidadãos tinham que recorrer diretamente aos tribunais para estas indemnizações, e os processos administrativos eram geralmente mais longos e complexos. Agora, ações administrativas de valor inferior a €15.000 terão um processo mais simples e rápido, com menos formalidades. A medida visa reduzir a pendência de processos nos tribunais administrativos e fiscais, que em 2025 registava 152.000 processos em primeira instância, com uma taxa de resolução de apenas 34%.
• **Lei da Representação de Interesses (Lei do Lobby):** O Presidente da República promulgou o Decreto da Assembleia da República que estabelece a orgânica do Registo de Transparência da Representação de Interesses. Esta lei, que entra em vigor a 27 de julho de 2026, impõe novas obrigações de transparência para empresas e outras entidades que interagem com decisores públicos, exigindo o registo das suas atividades de representação de interesses. Anteriormente, não existia um quadro legal abrangente para a atividade de lobby. A nova lei visa aumentar a transparência e a responsabilidade na interação entre entidades privadas e o Estado.
• **Decreto-Lei n.º 148/2026 (Ação Social no Ensino Superior):** Publicado em 20 de julho de 2026, este Decreto-Lei define os princípios e um novo modelo para a política de ação social escolar no ensino superior. O novo modelo visa promover a igualdade de oportunidades no acesso e frequência do ensino superior, através de apoios sociais diretos (bolsas de estudo) e indiretos (residências estudantis, apoio psicológico e adaptação para estudantes com necessidades educativas especiais). O diploma revoga despachos anteriores e altera a Lei n.º 71/2017, de 16 de agosto, que estabelece os preços máximos de refeição e alojamento para estudantes do ensino superior.
• **Portaria n.º 306/2026/1 (Condições de Trabalho de Administrativos):** Publicada em 22 de julho de 2026, esta Portaria procede à oitava alteração da Portaria n.º 182/2018, de 22 de junho, que regula as condições de trabalho dos trabalhadores administrativos não abrangidos por regulamentação coletiva específica. A alteração atualiza a tabela salarial, refletindo o aumento do valor da Retribuição Mínima Mensal Garantida (RMMG) para 2026, previsto no Acordo Tripartido Sobre Valorização Salarial e Crescimento Económico 2025-2028. Anteriormente, a tabela salarial não refletia o valor atualizado da RMMG de 2026. A medida assegura a diferenciação salarial equilibrada nos níveis remuneratórios subsequentes ao mínimo.
• **Medidas do Pacote Fiscal da Habitação (Entrada em vigor a 1 de setembro de 2026):** Embora o Decreto-Lei n.º 97/2026 tenha sido publicado em 20 de maio de 2026, algumas das suas medidas mais significativas para o fomento da oferta de habitação entram em vigor a 1 de setembro de 2026. Entre elas, destacam-se a implementação do Regime Simplificado de Arrendamento Acessível (RSAA) e os Contratos de Investimento para Arrendamento (CIA), que preveem benefícios fiscais (como isenções de IMT, IMI, AIMI e Imposto do Selo) por um período de até 25 anos para investidores que construam ou reabilitem imóveis para arrendamento com rendas moderadas (até €2.300/mês). Estes regimes visam aumentar a oferta de habitação no mercado de arrendamento a preços acessíveis.

Why it matters: As aprovações e entradas em vigor desta semana demonstram um foco contínuo do Governo na reforma da justiça para torná-la mais eficiente, na promoção da transparência nas relações entre privados e o Estado, e na melhoria das condições de vida e de trabalho, com especial atenção à ação social no ensino superior e a um incentivo mais forte à oferta de habitação no mercado.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Section 301 Tariffs on Goods Produced with Forced Labor:** On July 23, 2026, President Trump directed the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to impose additional duties of 10% or 12.5% ad valorem on all products from 60 economies found to have failed to prohibit or effectively enforce bans on imports made with forced labor. These tariffs became effective on July 24, 2026, at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time, with a limited in-transit exemption for goods loaded before July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption before July 28, 2026. Previously, such broad, forced-labor-related tariffs under Section 301 were not in place on a near-global basis; now, affected imports from nearly all major U.S. trading partners are subject to these new tariffs. This action signals a significant shift in global trade policy, increasing import costs for numerous goods and potentially reconfiguring supply chains for U.S. businesses.

• **Executive Order on Securing America's Defense Supply Chains:** On July 20, 2026, President Trump signed Executive Order 14415, "Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials," strengthening prohibitions on defense contractors from acquiring critical materials from foreign adversary countries. The order directs the Department of Defense (referred to as the Department of War) to develop policies within 180 days requiring all contractors supporting national security to map their supply chains back to raw material origin, vet suppliers for various risks (e.g., financial uncertainty, foreign ownership/control/influence, sole-sourcing), and implement mitigation plans, with authorization to use AI for this mapping. Previously, comprehensive supply chain mapping and strict vetting requirements for defense contractors at all tiers, tied to raw material origin and risks, were not uniformly mandated by executive order. This directive will increase scrutiny on defense industrial base supply chains, likely driving domestic sourcing and impacting contractors' operational costs and supplier relationships.

• **Section 301 Tariffs on Brazilian Imports:** On July 20, 2026, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) formally imposed an additional 25% ad valorem duty on a substantial volume of imports from Brazil, effective July 22, 2026, at 12:01 a.m. ET. This action concludes a year-long Section 301 investigation into Brazil's acts, policies, and practices related to digital trade, electronic payment services, preferential tariffs, ethanol market access, anti-corruption enforcement, intellectual property protection, and illegal deforestation. Previously, these specific imports from Brazil were not subject to these additional duties; now, U.S. importers face increased costs, with a limited in-transit exemption for goods loaded before July 22, 2026, and entered before July 29, 2026. This tariff increase will directly impact U.S. businesses importing goods from Brazil, potentially leading to higher consumer prices or shifts in sourcing.

• **Treasury Sanctions on Iranian Sanctions Evasion Network:** On July 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated four individuals and nine entities linked to Iranian financier Babak Zanjani, accusing his network of evading sanctions through financial services, digital asset trading, and other commercial activities. This action targets Zanjani's Iran-based "Dot One" conglomerate and associated firms in Turkey and the United Arab Emirates. These individuals and entities are now subject to asset blocking and prohibitions on transactions with U.S. persons. This broadens the U.S. campaign of economic pressure against Iran, further complicating financial and trade dealings for any entities involved with the designated network.

Why it matters: This week saw a significant escalation in U.S. trade policy through the widespread imposition of Section 301 tariffs, particularly the novel, near-global tariffs targeting forced labor enforcement, signaling a robust and expansive use of trade remedies to influence international labor and economic practices.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Moonshot AI Kimi K3:** Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 24, 2026, a multimodal, open-weights AI model featuring 2.8 trillion total parameters (50 billion active) and a one-million-token context window. This model achieves state-of-the-art performance in front-end development and web engineering, ranking #1 on the WebDev arena, and shows strong performance on coding benchmarks like DeepSWE (67.5%) and SWE Marathon (42%), rivaling Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, at a competitive API price of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Developers can now utilize this powerful, open-weights model for complex and long-horizon coding tasks, agentic knowledge work, and autonomous execution, significantly boosting efficiency in web development workflows.

• **AMD Hyperloom (part of ROCm.ai):** AMD shipped Hyperloom on July 23, 2026, an open-source, agentic system integrated within ROCm.ai, specifically designed to automate the optimization of end-to-end AI inference workloads. Hyperloom handles profiling, analysis, kernel optimization, and validation, demonstrating significant inference (3.3x) and training (2.4x) improvements over AMD's ROCm 7 on the same hardware. This enables developers working with AMD hardware to drastically reduce the time spent on specialized engineering for inference workload optimization from weeks to mere hours, accelerating AI application deployment.

• **Notion:** On July 24, 2026, Notion rolled out enhanced AI agent capabilities with the release of "Workers," allowing teams to collaboratively build, iterate on, and share custom multi-agent workflows directly within Notion's workspace. This update extends Notion 3.6's External Agents feature by enabling seamless integration and task assignment for agents like Claude and Cursor from shared boards, effectively creating a unified environment for automated processes. Knowledge workers can now automate complex, multi-step business processes by orchestrating various AI agents, including external ones, turning organizational knowledge embedded in documents and workflows into active, collaborative automation.

Why it matters: The AI landscape continues its rapid shift towards deployable, specialized, and cost-efficient solutions, with major players releasing advanced open-weights models and productivity tools that facilitate complex agentic workflows for developers and knowledge workers alike.
